Population = the three devices; NOT_RUN excludes all three. Gated by --selftest (15 assertions over the status map, no browser).

tools/withdraw-fragment-verdict.mjs.note: withdraws a verdict that judged a FRAGMENT of one recording, with its reason recorded (NIGHT-IS-THE-RECORDING-2026-10-05 §6). The object is per RUN, not per verdict: `checked` is how many withdrawal records were written, `eligible` every *-VERDICT.json in the fragment folder, `excluded` the ones skipped with a named reason (already withdrawn, or unreadable — an unreadable verdict is REFUSED rather than withdrawn with an empty body). A DRY RUN is NOT_RUN with result null and checked 0, every candidate excluded by the dry run itself: the withdrawal is what this gate measures and a dry run does not attempt it, so the would-write list goes to stdout as prose instead of into an object that claims to have measured. A second --apply over an already-withdrawn folder is NOT_APPLICABLE, also result null. PASS only when records were actually written. `--verdict-sample` runs the selftest's in-memory fixture — no corpus read, nothing written — so the adoption command does not depend on a night being present, the same reason corpus-census.mjs carries one.
